title: SRM College of Nursing Holds Lamp Lighting Ceremony for New B.Sc. Nursing and DGNM Batches
summary: SRM College of Nursing in Chennai welcomed its 35th B.Sc. Nursing and 34th DGNM batches with a Lamp Lighting Ceremony attended by Tmt. K. Porkodi, IAS.
body_html:
Chennai, 29 October 2026: SRM College of Nursing, part of SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), held its Lamp Lighting Ceremony 2026–2027 at SRM Medical College for the 35th batch of B.Sc. Nursing students and the 34th batch of Diploma in General Nursing and Midwifery (DGNM) students. The ceremony marks the start of the students’ professional journey in nursing and healthcare.

Tmt. K. Porkodi, IAS, Additional Director, Social Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, was the Chief Guest, while Dr. T. Mythili, Additional Registrar, MSL, SRMIST, presided over the event. The occasion is seen as an important milestone in a nursing student’s academic life, symbolising commitment to the profession and to the values of compassionate care and service.

The programme opened with an invocation, after which Prof. (Dr.) J. C. Helen Shaji, Dean, SRM College of Nursing, delivered the welcome address and felicitated the Chief Guest. The dignitaries lit the traditional lamp, and nursing personnel then lit the lamps held by the students.

Mrs. Ambiga, Associate Professor, SRM College of Nursing, explained the significance of the lamp lighting tradition. Mrs. Kavitha S., Chief Nursing Officer, SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, administered the Florence Nightingale Pledge, through which the students reaffirmed their commitment to professional ethics and patient care. First-year B.Sc. Nursing students also presented a dedication song.

Prof. (Dr.) J. C. Helen Shaji presented the college’s annual report, outlining its activities and achievements over the year. The felicitation session featured Dr. R. Venkatraman, Medical Superintendent, SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre.

Dr. T. Mythili gave the Presidential Address, which was followed by the Chief Guest Address. Tmt. K. Porkodi described nursing as a profession rooted in service, compassion and responsibility. She spoke of the calmness, empathy and resilience needed to care for patients in challenging situations, and of the role nurses play in giving patients hope, comfort and confidence during difficult times.

She urged the students to uphold professional ethics, to approach their responsibilities with dedication and to remember the human impact of the care they provide. According to the college, the ceremony reflects its commitment to preparing future nursing professionals with a strong sense of responsibility, compassion and dedication to patient care.
